purpose: Teach: 言いよう/腐っ/しつこく/概ね/受けとめ/取り消し/ふたたび/大嫌い

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんの言いように驚いたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, I was startled by the way your father spoke.
lines.style: Quiet, reflective opening. Gaze drawn inward to a memory. Measured pace, deliberate. The word 「驚いた」lands with small, genuine weight — not dramatic, just honest surprise revisited.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、腐ったお魚を絶対に食べさせなかったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mm-hmm, and you — you never let us eat spoiled fish, did you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, slightly teasing affection. Gentle correction wrapped in agreement. Her memory is different from his, and she says so kindly. A lift at the end — not quite a question, more a companionable nudge.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、近所がしつこく訪ねてきたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, the neighbors kept showing up at our door.
lines.style: Same reflective distance as before. Steady, unhurried. The word 「しつこく」comes without complaint — just stating what happened. Eyes still on the memory, not the present moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お話が概ね正しいと納得されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you — you accepted what I told you, didn't you, dear? Mostly.
lines.style: Tender patience. She's gently amending his version again. Not correcting harshly — more like settling in beside him, saying 'well, yes, but here's what I remember.' A quiet smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お祖父ちゃんが私の悩みを真摯に受けとめてくれたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father — he really took my worries seriously.
lines.style: Tender weight on this one. The gratitude is quiet but unmistakable. 「真摯に」is the heart of it — delivered with the kind of warmth that comes from old appreciation. Still measured, but gentler now.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご予約の取り消しは丁寧になさったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you — you handled canceling that reservation so kindly, didn't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, almost playful affection. She's offering her own memory, her own version of kindness. Not dismissing his, just saying 'yes, and you did kind things too.' A slight brightness in her tone — she's fond of him, and it shows.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとふたたびあの場所を訪ねたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, your father and I went back to that place again.
lines.style: The memory settles deeper now. Slower pace. A sense of something unresolved or cherished being revisited. 「ふたたび」holds weight — the return mattered. Voice slightly distant, tender with the weight of years.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、辛いものが大嫌いだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you — you've always hated spicy food, haven't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm, intimate, gently teasing affection. She's saying something smaller now — a daily, lived detail. Closer to him. Trailing softly, like a small smile that's been there the whole conversation. The 「わよね」is fond and certain.
